conflicts.quote: The cadence figure comes from the wire (a `refresh_seconds`-style field), never hardcoded in FE copy — a hardcoded "every 60s" goes stale the day the poll changes.
conflicts.why: No poll cadence exists in v1 (on-demand fetch + short server TTL cache + explicit user refresh; background poller is a named deferred seam). A refresh_seconds field would put a scheduled-refresh claim on the wire that no scheduler backs; dependent copy inherits the fiction.
conflicts.proposal: Envelope carries as_of + basis (fresh vs served-from-cache) + a server-supplied max-staleness datum derived from the TTL. UX rewrites affected strings to on-demand truth. Cadence field + original copy return together with the v2 poller.

conflicts.quote: The cadence figure comes from the wire (a `refresh_seconds`-style field), never hardcoded in FE copy — a hardcoded "every 60s" goes stale the day the poll changes.
conflicts.why: Same conflict as C1a from the product side: copy promising automatic refresh the product never performs is a freshness fabrication — never-auto-refreshing data presented as scheduled.
conflicts.proposal: v1 provenance copy states the on-demand basis; staleness renders from as-of age against a server-declared threshold, never a cadence. AC-7/AC-11 language follows the on-demand framing.

conflicts.quote: **Webull · read-only**  ·  `as of 2:41:07 PM`  ·  refreshes about every {cadence} — a snapshot, never live.
conflicts.why: Own-lane copy self-falsified by the architect's refresh model, surfaced rather than silently patched. Same root as C1a/C1b; also infects S6 trigger, S7 'this cycle', and PM AC-11.
conflicts.proposal: Header: 'Webull · read-only · as of {time} · read on demand — a snapshot, never live.' S6 keys off an explicit age threshold; S7: 'Couldn't reach Webull just now — showing your book as of {time}.'

conflicts.quote: **AC-6** *(blocked-on-approval; verified in the named runtime follow-up)* With a connected broker and a non-empty Webull book, the Live tab lists the owner's actual positions — symbols and quantities matching what the Webull app shows — with a multi-leg options position rendered as one position with its legs, not N unrelated rows.
conflicts.why: Commits pre-capture to a payload capability the BRIEF orders treated as OPEN. If Webull reports options per-contract flat with no grouping identity, 'one position with its legs' requires heuristic composition — the same class of fabrication AC-14 forbids in the flattening direction.
conflicts.proposal: Split: AC-6a unconditional (every reported holding appears; symbols/quantities match; count never understates). AC-6b conditional on capture (grouping identity present ⇒ legs render grouped; flat payload ⇒ the rendering fallback is a named post-capture PRODUCT decision for the owner).

conflicts.quote: **PM treats the blocked Webull approval as a sequencing fact** (payload capture is build task #1; design proceeds now), not as a reason to ship an unverified adapter behind a flag or to invent a mock-only "done." Falsified if the PM's definition of done doesn't include a live payload capture.
conflicts.why: Quietly decides a ship-timing question that is the owner's: if approval outlasts the build, 'done requires live capture' holds GATE S hostage to a third party. Ship-19/20-with-AC-6-deferred vs hold-for-capture is a priority call.
conflicts.proposal: Keep capture as build task #1; if approval lags at GATE Q, the conductor presents the owner an explicit either/or rather than either lane pre-deciding.

conflicts.quote: **AC-8** A manual refresh affordance exists; using it updates the as-of stamp on success.
conflicts.why: Under throttle+TTL a refresh can honestly serve the cache — a success whose stamp does not move. As written AC-8 either fails on the honest cache-serve or forces bypassing the throttle protecting the owner's broker rate limits.
conflicts.proposal: Reword AC-8: refresh either advances the stamp or visibly states the snapshot came from cache and why (throttled / broker unreachable) — never a silent no-op.

conflicts.quote: Rate limiting is handled server-side (throttle + TTL cache); a rate-limited moment serves the cached book with its honest `as_of`/`basis`, or `unknown` if there is none.
conflicts.why: Incomplete envelope story: with a valid cache an outage becomes invisible — only signal is an old as_of. Stale (nobody asked recently) and degraded (last attempt FAILED) are different honesty claims and trader actions; AC-12/S7 become unrenderable. Also last-known rows after cache expiry exist only in client session memory, so 'your last confirmed book stays below' is conditionally true.
conflicts.proposal: Additive fields on BrokerBook: last_attempt_at + closed last_attempt_outcome (ok | broker_unreachable | rate_limited | credential_rejected | adapter_fault). S7/S8 'last-known book' clauses become conditional on a confirmed same-session book.
